I have resolved the issue in [related_descriptors.py](file:///tmp/xhs-c6-host-va4tl0hw/django/db/models/fields/related_descriptors.py).

### Cause
When prefetching related objects via [`ForwardManyToOneDescriptor.get_prefetch_queryset()`](file:///tmp/xhs-c6-host-va4tl0hw/django/db/models/fields/related_descriptors.py#L120-L150), [`ReverseOneToOneDescriptor.get_prefetch_queryset()`](file:///tmp/xhs-c6-host-va4tl0hw/django/db/models/fields/related_descriptors.py#L365-L383), or [`RelatedManager.get_prefetch_queryset()`](file:///tmp/xhs-c6-host-va4tl0hw/django/db/models/fields/related_descriptors.py#L635-L655), iterating over `queryset` evaluates nested `prefetch_related()`/`select_related()` lookups on the related objects first, populating their reverse relation cache. Afterward, `get_prefetch_queryset()` unconditionally set the reverse relation cache on each `rel_obj` to the parent `instance`, overwriting the already-cached inner instance (and its loaded/deferred fields).

### Solution
Check whether the relation is already cached on `rel_obj` (`is_cached(rel_obj)`) before setting the reverse relation cache to `instance` in:
- [`ForwardManyToOneDescriptor.get_prefetch_queryset()`](file:///tmp/xhs-c6-host-va4tl0hw/django/db/models/fields/related_descriptors.py#L145-L149)
- [`ReverseOneToOneDescriptor.get_prefetch_queryset()`](file:///tmp/xhs-c6-host-va4tl0hw/django/db/models/fields/related_descriptors.py#L379-L382)
- [`RelatedManager.get_prefetch_queryset()`](file:///tmp/xhs-c6-host-va4tl0hw/django/db/models/fields/related_descriptors.py#L650-L653)
